newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: IMF approves loan disbursement for Kazakhstan.
newsitem.headline: IMF approves loan disbursement for Kazakhstan.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund has approved the disbursement of part of a $446 million loan to the former Soviet republic of Kazakhstan, a fund official said on Monday.

David Hoelscher, the IMF's resident representative in the Kazakh capital Almaty, told Reuters the disbursement was agreed at Kazakhstan's first review meeting in Washington last month, which said economic reforms were on course.
Hoelscher did not say what sum was disbursed, explaining that the Kazakh government had so far not drawn on the three-year extended fund facility agreed in July last year.
"Thus far the government has not drawn on its funds because of the strong reserve position of the National Bank," Hoelscher said.
The government of the natural resource-rich republic is aiming at economic growth of around two percent this year, up from 0.5 percent in 1996.
The republic also aims to cut annual inflation to 19 percent this year, from around 30 percent in 1996.
An IMF mission is due to visit Kazakhstan later this month, although a date has yet to be fixed.
